stem: For some value of \(t\), the point \((4, t)\) is a solution to the system of inequalities below, where \(c\) is a constant. \[ y > 3x + c \] \[ y < -x + 2 \] What is the greatest integer value of \(c\) for which this is possible?
solution: Substitute \(x = 4\): the system becomes \(t > 12 + c\) and \(t < -2\).
Some value of \(t\) satisfies both exactly when \(12 + c < -2\), that is, \(c < -14\).
The inequality is strict, so \(c = -14\) does not work (then \(t > -2\) and \(t < -2\)). The greatest integer value is \(-15\).
verify:
c, t = symbols('c t')
lo, hi = 3*4 + c, -4 + 2
cond = solve_univariate_inequality(lo < hi, c, relational=False)
assert cond == Interval.open(-oo, -14)
best = max(k for k in range(-40, 10) if k in cond)
assert best == -15 and [Rational(a) for a in spr_answers] == [best]
